title_en: On the So-Called Gospel of Peter
author: Serapion of Antioch
occasion: Serapion writes to correct his earlier permission for the church at Rhossus to read a gospel attributed to Peter, after learning that it was being used to support Docetic teaching.
argument: Serapion affirms that he and the church receive Peter and the other apostles as they receive Christ, but reject writings falsely attributed to them. He recalls that during a visit to Rhossus he had allowed the reading of a gospel bearing Peter's name, assuming the church was orthodox. After learning that the community's mind was harboring heresy, he now plans to return quickly. He explains that he obtained the gospel from others who had studied it, that is, from the successors of those who had originated it, whom we call Docetists, and found that most of it agrees with the true teaching of the Savior, but some things have been added, which he lists for them.

outline.move: Serapion states the principle of receiving the apostles but rejecting pseudepigrapha, recounts his earlier permission regarding the Gospel of Peter, announces his coming visit, and explains how he examined the gospel and found mostly sound teaching with some Docetic additions.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Marcion... Heretic whose self-contradictory teaching Serapion mentions specifically as the type of heresy the Rhossus community's mind was harboring, not merely as a general example.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: καταλαβόμενοι ὁποίας ἦν αἱρέσεως ὁ Μαρκιανός, ὃς καὶ ἑαυτῷ ἠναντιοῦτο μὴ νοῶν ἃ ἐλάλει, ἃ μαθήσεσθε ἐξ ὧν ὑμῖν ἐγράφη
_unresolved_facts.fix: Marcion is mentioned as a general example of a heretic who contradicted himself, not specifically as the type of heresy the Rhossus community was harboring. The text says 'having understood of what sort was the heresy of Marcion, who also contradicted himself not understanding what he spoke, which things you will learn from what was written to you' — this is a parenthetical characterization of Marcion as a paradigmatic self-contradicting heretic, not an identification of the Rhossus community's heresy as specifically Marcionite. The community's heresy is identified as Docetic (ἐκ τῶν λεχθέντων μοι... αἱρέσει τινὶ ὁ νοῦς αὐτῶν ἐνεφώλευεν, and the gospel was obtained from Δοκητὰς).

_unresolved_facts.claim: He explains that he obtained the gospel from others who had studied it, that is, from the successors of those who had originated it, whom we call Docetists, and found that most of it agrees with the true teaching of the Savior, but some things have been added, which he lists for them.
_unresolved_facts.fix: The fragment states that Serapion 'subjoined/attached [them] to you' (ὑπετάξαμεν ὑμῖν), but the brief's claim that 'he lists for them' implies the list is present in this fragment. The fragment itself does not contain the list of additions; it only references that they were subjoined. The brief should clarify that the list is not preserved in this fragment.

_unresolved_facts.claim: after learning that it was being used to support Docetic teaching
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: νῦν δὲ μαθὼν ὅτι αἱρέσει τινὶ ὁ νοῦς αὐτῶν ἐνεφώλευεν
_unresolved_facts.fix: The source says he learned that 'their mind was harboring/nestling in some heresy' (αἱρέσει τινὶ ὁ νοῦς αὐτῶν ἐνεφώλευεν), not specifically that the gospel was being used to support Docetic teaching. The Docetic connection comes from Serapion's later investigation of the text's origins, not from the initial report about the community.
